title: Stitching It Together: From Frames to a 3D Scene
throughline: Turning captured frames into a reconstruction: equirectangular/360 stitching from dual-fisheye, feature matching, COLMAP structure-from-motion pose recovery, bundle adjustment, Gaussian-splat (gsplat) training, loop closure, registration diagnostics, and the bundle/manifest data contract.
rationale: A well-captured bundle still needs a deterministic path — stitch, match, pose, train — turning frames into a scene, and that path's diagnostics are what tell the field side whether the capture actually worked.
research_seeds: COLMAP automatic_reconstructor command line documentation — COLMAP official docs
COLMAP feature_extractor and matcher options for sequential indoor imagery — COLMAP official docs
3D Gaussian Splatting for Real-Time Radiance Field Rendering — Kerbl et al. 2023 paper
gsplat training pipeline and API — gsplat / Nerfstudio project documentation
equirectangular projection format and 2:1 aspect ratio spec — panoramic/360 imaging standards
Insta360 dual-fisheye stitching SDK and equirectangular export — Insta360 developer documentation
bundle adjustment in structure from motion explained — Hartley & Zisserman, Multiple View Geometry
COLMAP sparse reconstruction registration statistics and output format — COLMAP official docs
loop closure detection in structure-from-motion pipelines — SfM/SLAM research literature
COLMAP model_converter and camera pose visualization (PLY/COLMAP GUI) — COLMAP official docs
Python zipfile and JSON manifest schema design for data bundles — Python standard library documentation
NeRF and Gaussian splatting baseline/parallax requirements, degenerate rotation-only capture — 3DGS/NeRF papers
COLMAP incremental mapping vs. global SfM pipeline comparison — COLMAP official docs
panorama stitching quality validation: width, height, and aspect ratio checks — imaging QA references
